summary: Join our specialized training course on derivatives in monetary policy and financial stability. Gain essential skills to navigate complex financial landscapes.
lede: Derivatives training explains how these markets transmit risk and liquidity for policy, supervisory, and risk professionals. It covers futures, forwards, swaps, and options, including how interest-rate and foreign-exchange derivatives inform policy analysis. Participants practise interpreting exposures and margin demands, assessing clearing and interconnectedness, and incorporating interest-rate, currency, and credit shocks into stress tests and financial-stability decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for a diverse group of professionals who interact with derivatives from a policy, oversight, strategy, or risk management perspective.
audience: Financial stability and macroprudential policy teams
Treasury and risk management professionals in commercial
Analysts in policy think tanks and international
modules: Foundations of Derivatives in Modern Financial Systems
Interest Rate Derivatives and Monetary Policy Transmission
Foreign Exchange Derivatives and Exchange Rate Management
Credit and Equity Derivatives in Financial Stability Analysis
Clearing, Margining, and Market Infrastructure for Stability
Regulatory Frameworks for Derivatives and Systemic Risk
Integrating Derivatives into Stress Testing and Scenario Analysis
Derivatives, Macroprudential Policy, and Risk Mitigation
Communicating Derivatives Risks to Policy Makers and Stakeholders
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of financial markets and instruments. Prior experience in financial policy, regulation, or risk management is beneficial but not required.
